'''''Eucalyptus sideroxylon''''', commonly known as '''mugga ironbark''',<ref name="RBGS">{{cite web |last1=Hill |first1=Ken |title=''Eucalyptus sideroxylon'' |url=http://plantnet.rbgsyd.nsw.gov.au/cgi-bin/NSWfl.pl?page=nswfl&lvl=sp&name=Eucalyptus~sideroxylon |publisher=Royal Botanic Garden Sydney |access-date=22 December 2019 |archive-date=19 August 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230819152413/https://plantnet.rbgsyd.nsw.gov.au/cgi-bin/NSWfl.pl?page=nswfl&lvl=sp&name=Eucalyptus~sideroxylon |url-status=live }}</ref> or '''red ironbark'''<ref name="RBGV">{{cite web |last1=Brooker |first1=M. Ian H. |last2=Slee |first2=Andrew V. |title=''Eucalyptus sideroxylon'' |url=https://vicflora.rbg.vic.gov.au/flora/taxon/b967c639-c30e-4bdd-8f78-f8c903134f5c |publisher=Royal Botanic Gardens, Victoria |access-date=23 December 2019 |archive-date=23 December 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191223061353/https://vicflora.rbg.vic.gov.au/flora/taxon/b967c639-c30e-4bdd-8f78-f8c903134f5c |url-status=live }}</ref> is a small to medium-sized tree that is [[Endemism|endemic]] to eastern Australia. It has dark, deeply furrowed [[ironbark]], lance-shaped adult leaves, flower buds in groups of seven, white, red, pink or creamy yellow flowers and cup-shaped to shortened spherical fruit.

==Description==
''Eucalyptus sideroxylon'' is a tree that typically grows to a height of {{cvt|25-35|m}} and forms a [[lignotuber]]. The bark is dark grey to black, deeply furrowed ironbark on the trunk and larger branches, smooth white to grey on the thinnest branches. Young plants and [[coppice]] regrowth have lance-shaped to oblong or linear leaves that are {{cvt|30-110|mm}} long and {{cvt|5-35|mm}} wide. Adult leaves are lance-shaped, the same shade of green on both sides, {{cvt|50-140|mm}} long and {{cvt|10-40|mm}} wide tapering to a [[Petiole (botany)|petiole]] {{cvt|5-25|mm}} long. The flower buds are arranged in leaf [[wikt:axil|axil]]s on an unbranched [[Peduncle (botany)|peduncle]] {{cvt|7-29|mm}} long, the individual buds on [[Pedicel (botany)|pedicels]] {{cvt|3-15|mm}} long. Mature buds are oval or diamond-shaped, {{cvt|6-15|mm}} long and {{cvt|4-6|mm}} wide with a conical to beaked [[Operculum (botany)|operculum]]. Flowering occurs from April to December and the flowers are white, red, pink or creamy yellow. The fruit is a woody cup-shaped to shortened spherical [[Capsule (botany)|capsule]] {{cvt|5-11|mm}} long and {{cvt|5-10|mm}} wide with the valves below the level of the rim.<ref name="RBGS" /><ref name="CANBR">{{cite web |title=''Eucalyptus sideroxylon'' |url=https://apps.lucidcentral.org/euclid/text/entities/eucalyptus_sideroxylon.htm |publisher=Euclid: Centre for Australian National Biodiversity Research |access-date=29 May 2020 |archive-date=22 June 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210622110641/https://apps.lucidcentral.org/euclid/text/entities/eucalyptus_sideroxylon.htm |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name="ABRS">{{cite web |last1=Chippendale |first1=George M. |title=''Eucalyptus sideroxylon'' |url=https://profiles.ala.org.au/opus/foa/profile/Eucalyptus%20sideroxylon |publisher=Australian Biological Resources Study, Department of the Environment and Energy, Canberra |access-date=23 December 2019 |archive-date=19 August 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230819152410/https://profiles.ala.org.au/opus/foa/profile/Eucalyptus%20sideroxylon |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name="RBGV2">{{cite web |last1=Messina |first1=Andre |last2=Stajsic |first2=Val |title=''Eucalyptus sideroxylon'' subsp. ''sideroxylon'' |url=https://vicflora.rbg.vic.gov.au/flora/taxon/018f3a83-d75d-42da-8047-faf278a3cbbe |publisher=Royal Botanic Gardens, Victoria |access-date=23 December 2019 |archive-date=23 December 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191223061346/https://vicflora.rbg.vic.gov.au/flora/taxon/018f3a83-d75d-42da-8047-faf278a3cbbe |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name=dn>{{cite web|url=https://www.australiangeographic.com.au/topics/science-environment/2010/04/guide-to-australias-gum-blossoms/|title=An illustrated guide to Australia's gum blossoms|author=Dean Nicolle|publisher=Australian Geographic|date=30 April 2010|access-date=19 November 2017|author-link=Dean Nicolle|archive-date=17 November 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171117095328/http://www.australiangeographic.com.au/topics/science-environment/2010/04/guide-to-australias-gum-blossoms|url-status=live}}</ref>

==Taxonomy and naming==
[[Allan Cunningham (botanist)|Allan Cunningham]] recorded the name ''Eucalyptus sideroxylon'' in [[Thomas Mitchell (explorer)|Thomas Mitchell]]'s 1848 ''Journal of an Expedition into the Interior of Tropical Australia'' but did not provide a description of the plant. The first formal description of the species was published in 1887 by [[William Woolls]] in ''[[Linnean Society of New South Wales|Proceedings of the Linnean Society of New South Wales]]''.<ref name=APNI>{{cite web|title=''Eucalyptus sideroxylon''|url=https://id.biodiversity.org.au/instance/apni/455139|publisher=APNI|access-date=23 December 2019|archive-date=19 August 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230819152414/https://biodiversity.org.au/nsl/services/rest/instance/apni/455139|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="Woolls">{{cite journal |last1=Woolls |first1=William |title=Notes on ''Eucalyptus leucoxylon'' (Series 2) |journal=Proceedings of the Linnean Society of New South Wales |date=1887 |volume=1 |pages=859–860 |url=https://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/item/30467#page/891/mode/1up |access-date=23 December 2019 |archive-date=20 July 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190720135031/https://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/item/30467#page/891/mode/1up |url-status=live }}</ref> The [[Botanical name|specific epithet]] (''sideroxylon'') is derived from the [[ancient Greek]] words {{Lang|grc-Latn|sidēros}} ({{Lang|grc|σίδηρος}}), meaning "iron" and {{Lang|grc-Latn|xylon}} ({{Lang|grc|ξύλον}}), meaning "wood".<ref name="Backer">Backer, C.A. (1936). ''Verklarend woordenboek der wetenschappelijke namen van de in Nederland en Nederlandsch-Indië in het wild groeiende en in tuinen en parken gekweekte varens en hoogere planten'' (Edition Nicoline van der Sijs).</ref>

Two subspecies of ''E. sideroxylon'' are accepted by the [[Australian Plant Census]] as at December 2019:

* ''Eucalyptus sideroxylon'' <small>A.Cunn. ex Woolls</small> subsp. ''sideroxylon''.<ref name=APC2>{{cite web|title=''Eucalyptus sideroxylon'' subsp. ''sideroxylon''|url=https://biodiversity.org.au/nsl/services/apc-format/display/77044|publisher=Australian Plant Census|access-date=23 December 2019|archive-date=23 December 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191223061343/https://biodiversity.org.au/nsl/services/apc-format/display/77044|url-status=live}}</ref>

==Distribution and habitat==
Mugga ironbark is widespread and often abundant in woodland from south-eastern Queensland through New South Wales to Victoria. Subspecies ''improcera'' is only known from the Barakula State Forest north-northwest of [[Chinchilla, Queensland|Chinchilla]].<ref name="RBGS" /><ref name="CANBR" /><ref name="JSTOR" /> 

==Uses==
The leaves are used in the production of [[cineole]] based [[eucalyptus oil]].<ref>Boland, D.J., Brophy, J.J., and A.P.N. House, ''Eucalyptus Leaf Oils'', 1991, {{ISBN|0-909605-69-6}}</ref>

[[Apiarist]]s in New South Wales place hives in red-ironbark woodlands to collect the [[honey]].<ref name=dn/>

==Chemistry==
Molecules produced by plants in case of pathogens attacks are called [[phytoalexin]]s. Such compounds can be implied in the [[hypersensitive response]] of plants. High levels of polyphenols ([[stilbenoid]]s and [[ellagitannin]]s) in ''E. sideroxylon'' wood can explain its natural [[wood preservation|preservation]] against rot.<ref>{{cite journal |title=Inhibition of wood-rotting fungi by stilbenes and other polyphenols in Eucalyptus sideroxylon |first1=John H. |last1=Hart |first2=W. E. |last2=Hillis |journal=Phytopathology |volume=64 |pages=939–48 |year=1974 |doi=10.1094/Phyto-64-939 |issue=7}}</ref>
